title: Testing the Compiler (Trivial Type Invariants)
pattern: A test written to verify basic properties guaranteed by the language compiler, type system, or standard library (such as type assignment, basic struct derivation, or basic map behavior).
why_bad: It adds zero confidence while cluttering the test suite with boilerplate that must be maintained [32]. It is a waste of execution and engineering time [274].
detection: Assertions checking language standard library behavior or basic compiler-generated struct properties directly.
counterexample: Verifying custom trait implementations or complex manual implementations of structural equality that override standard behaviors.
fix: Delete the trivial tests and trust the language compiler and runtime properties [32, 274].
source: *   *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, "Mechanical Facts / Language invariants" (p. 274) [32]
